aircraft.engine: CFM LEAP-1A or Pratt & Whitney PW1100G-JM
aircraft.source: Limits (Mmo 0.82, typical cruise Mach 0.78, service ceiling 39,800 ft) corroborated across multiple independent sources including Airbus-derived specification summaries. Climb/cruise/descent profile ADAPTED from SKYbrary's published A321(ceo) indicative performance data (cruise TAS 450kt/M0.79 at FL410; initial descent to FL240 at M0.78/1000fpm; descent to FL100 at 290 KIAS/2500fpm) — the neo shares the ceo's airframe aerodynamics with re-engined, more efficient powerplants, so profile shape is expected to be very similar despite the source being for the ceo variant specifically.
aircraft.source_confidence: MODERATE. Limits are well corroborated for the neo specifically. The climb/descent PROFILE SHAPE is sourced (SKYbrary) but for the ceo variant, not the neo — treat this as a reasonable proxy, not a neo-specific certified figure.

climb.reference_condition: Typical airline climb profile, moderate weight, ISA. Speed schedule: 250 KIAS below FL100, ~300 KIAS climb, transitioning to Mach ~0.78.
climb.notes: Adapted from A321ceo typical profile; neo's more efficient LEAP-1A/PW1100G engines may produce modestly better climb performance at a given weight than the ceo's CFM56/V2500, which this table does not attempt to quantify.

cruise.reference_condition: Typical cruise, ISA — SKYbrary published data point (ceo): TAS 450kt/M0.79 at FL410
cruise.notes: 0.78 typical cruise Mach is the most consistently reported figure for the neo family specifically across independent sources.

descent.reference_condition: SKYbrary published descent profile (A321ceo, adapted): initial descent to FL240 at Mach 0.78/1000fpm; descent to FL100 at 290 KIAS/2500fpm.
descent.notes: Sourced from SKYbrary's A321(ceo) entry, not neo-specific. Blended single-value figure below combines the two published segments duration-weighted.
